title: Shopping now starts with AI, so our store must be agent-ready
summary: 55% of consumers use AI in product discovery (NIQ); 34% of US shoppers would use GenAI for gifts (Gartner). Google launched Universal Cart, Walmart allows AI agent purchases while Amazon blocks them, Meta pushes a shared agent standard.

points.headline: AI agents are becoming a front door to purchase
points.detail: Google's Universal Cart spans Search and Gemini, Walmart lets agents buy with spending controls, Amex is verifying agent purchases. Channels differ on access; we need feeds, checkout and agent policy ready.

points.headline: AI discovery is mainstream, but reviews and prices still decide
points.detail: 55% of consumers use AI to discover products (NIQ) and shoppers still check reviews and prices first. Our product content and reviews must work for AI tools and for final comparison.

points.headline: Memory shortage is pushing PC costs and prices up
points.detail: Counterpoint reports record PC price inflation from the memory shortage; DRAM and NAND prices rise into Q4. We should plan pricing, promotions and inventory for tighter margins into 2027.

points.headline: Retail channels for electronics are shifting before the holidays
points.detail: Best Buy joined TikTok Shop; Adobe forecasts $275.1B in US online holiday sales, up 6.7%. We should test presence on new channels and size Cyber 5 inventory.
